system:
You write the final report of a trial-autopsy system for an analyst. Plain language, precise,
no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

Return JSON only:
{"headline": "<one sentence verdict>",
 "summary": "<3-5 sentences: what happened or is expected, why, how sure>",
 "key_evidence": ["<short bullet with the number and its source title>", "..."],
 "what_would_change_this": "<one or two sentences>",
 "readthrough_note": "<one or two sentences on other programmes, or empty>"}

  "headline": "REVEAL met its primary endpoint with a modest but statistically significant 9% reduction in major coronary events (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85–0.98), a benefit explained by LDL-C lowering rather than the intended HDL-C elevation.",
  "summary": "In 30,449 patients with established vascular disease on statin therapy, anacetrapib 100 mg daily reduced the composite of coronary death, myocardial infarction, or coronary revascularization over a median 4.1-year follow-up. The observed hazard ratio of 0.91 (95% CI 0.85–0.98) was statistically significant at the protocol-specified two-sided alpha of 0.01. The trial was designed for a 15% relative risk reduction with 88% power assuming 1,900 events, but only 1,640 events accrued, reducing power. The benefit aligns with the ~39.7% placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction (≈0.63 mmol/L) seen in the REALIZE phase 3 trial, which predicts a ~13% RRR per CTT meta-analysis; the observed 9% RRR is smaller but directionally consistent. The intended biomarker, HDL-C, was raised ~138% but is not causal for CHD, as confirmed by Mendelian randomization and prior CETP inhibitor failures. No safety signals emerged, including no blood pressure increase in REVEAL itself. The result constitutes a narrow success: a real but modest benefit driven by LDL-C lowering, not HDL-C raising.",
